source_review.notes: Checked current AMD and Intel power-analysis guidance, the current IEEE Unified Power Format record, primary HotSpot and McPAT repositories, the OpenROAD physical-design project, author resources for digital architecture, and a current CMOS VLSI publisher record. All eight authoritative URLs returned HTTP 200. Power intent, tool and model capabilities, simplified arithmetic, physical practices and system recommendations remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked activity, capacitance, voltage, frequency, dynamic/leakage power, energy, useful work, temperature and thermal-resistance notation.
Verified power, energy, density, transient temperature and steady-state estimates remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Units are consistent across farads, volts, hertz, watts, seconds, joules and degrees Celsius per watt.

evidence: Recomputed dynamic power as 0.2*10e-9*0.8^2*1e9 = 1.280 W and total as 1.680 W.
Recomputed 0.5-second energy as 0.840 J and one-node steady junction as 40+12*1.68 = 60.16 C.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduced all four expected power, energy and temperature outputs.

evidence: Re-derived switching sensitivity as alpha*C*V^2*f and energy as the time integral of total power.
Checked the one-node steady thermal relation and identified absent spatial, transient and leakage-temperature feedback terms.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The equations are first-order conditional models and are not presented as transistor-, package- or workload-complete predictions.
